messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0022. Final outcome: refund_partial, amount $6.43 as a Ryde voucher. Account flag: no. Recommended action: Issue the rider a Ryde voucher of $6.43 (RD-2 meter mileage unit for the 4.56 km unexempted off-route segment); no account flag; retain the metered waiting unit and the rest of the $39.18 bill..
Reasoning:
RD-1 is satisfied: one gps off-route segment exists, F3 (21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, +4.56 km, up to 1958 m off route), and the whole trip ran 18.7 km against a 13.9 km optimal route (+4.8 km, +35%) [F1][F3]. Under RD-1 an unexplained off-route segment breaches the driver's duty to take the shortest and most direct route; no percentage or kilometre threshold applies.

RD-5 timing is met but the scope question is what decides the segment. The only rider message sent before the segment started (21:39, F3) is F9 at 21:36, which answers the driver's F8 request to "pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute". Read in its words, F9 is agreement to a one-minute stop at a station on the then-current line of travel — a stop request, not a route choice. Nothing in F8 or F9 names a road or area, so this is not a "specific named road" authorisation whose correspondence with the driven path could be tested (G13); and F11, a post-trip driver statement, cannot supply consent at all (G11). I therefore read the consent as covering a brief stop on the current route, not a 10-minute, 6.27 km loop running up to 1958 m off the optimal route [F8][F9][F11][F3][RD-5].

RD-3 does not rescue the segment either. RD-3(a) requires the rider to have named the place and the car to have stopped there; the rider named no place (F9 names no road or station) and the trace records no measured stop, so the whole-way-there exemption cannot attach; the mileage in F3 is left to RD-2 [F8][F9][RD-3]. On the record as given, the residual ambiguity is about how far the agreed stop extended, and 4.56 km of extra driving is outside any reading of "just ahead / one minute"; the segment accordingly counts.

RD-4 gives no excuse: no qualifying incident exists (✗ on the trace), F14 records none near the route, and the band-5 (40–49 km/h) records F12/F13 are not band 1 or 2 and cannot stand alone as a justification [F14][F12][F13][RD-4].

RD-2 (RydeTAXI branch) therefore applies and the refund is limited to the metered mileage unit of the unexempted segment: F4 states the trip's distance fare rate as $26.31 distance fare ÷ 18.66 km = $1.4100/km, and the unexempted segment added 4.56 km (F3), so 4.56 km × $1.4100/km = $6.4296 → $6.43. The remaining $0.34 by which the fare record's excess-distance line ($6.77 for 4.80 km vs 4.8 km optimal-route difference, F1/F4) exceeds this sum falls outside the off-route segment and is not refunded under RD-2's rule that mileage not assigned to any segment is not recoverable [F3][F4][F1][RD-2].

RD-6 is not engaged: the driver's 90-day profile shows 2 upheld disputes but 0 route disputes, so the "repeated route deviation" condition (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no account flag is added; the profile facts are used only for this additional-action question, never to decide the segment [F17][RD-6]. The metered waiting unit of $0.11 (F5, F7) is a RydeTAXI meter waiting unit and is not refundable [F5][RD-3].

Safety screen: I read F8, F9, F11 and the rider's complaint; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the "never stopped for petrol" wording is a factual complaint, not an abuse or a safety allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1]. Nothing required a safety escalation.

Evidence is sufficient: the chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F10), the trip is fully covered by gps and fare records (F1–F7), and the trace settles the RD-4 screen (✗) and the RD-6 screen (✗), so every element of this ruling is settled by the record [F10][F3][F4][F17][RD-2][RD-5].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments:
{"rider": "You get a $6.43 Ryde voucher. It covers the extra distance from the detour your driver took mid-trip: 4.56 km of driving that was off the direct route.

Your messages at the time only agreed to a quick stop at a petrol station, not a 10-minute detour of over 6 km. That is why the detour distance is refunded. The rest of your $39.18 fare, including the metered waiting time, stands, since no other part of the trip was found to be wrong.

No change is being made to the driver's account. The voucher is added to your Ryde account automatically.", "driver": "The dispute was partly upheld. A $6.43 Ryde voucher goes to the rider, covering 4.56 km of driving off the most direct route during a mid-trip detour. The rider's messages only agreed to a brief stop at a petrol station, so the longer detour distance is treated as unagreed. The rest of the $39.18 fare, including the metered waiting unit, is kept.

No flag or other action is placed on your account. This outcome is based on the trip's route and fare records and the messages exchanged during the trip."}
